records.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain and Dead Car Syndrome
records.description: The i5 (both eDrive40 and M60 xDrive) uses a small 12V auxiliary battery to power the vehicle computer systems, door locks, and startup sequence. Like other BMW EVs, the i5 can experience excessive 12V battery drain when the car is parked for extended periods (more than 3-5 days). Multiple connected services modules continue drawing power even in sleep mode, depleting the 12V battery. A dead 12V battery renders the car completely inoperable — you cannot open the doors, shift out of park, or engage the main HV battery.
records.solution: Keep the i5 plugged in when parked for extended periods — the HV charger trickle-charges the 12V battery. Install a BMW-recommended battery maintainer connected to the 12V battery (accessible in the right side of the trunk). Update iDrive software to the latest version — BMW has released OTA updates that improve sleep-mode power management. If the 12V battery dies, the manual release cable under the hood allows emergency access.
symptoms: Car will not unlock with key fob after sitting several days
Drivetrain Malfunction warning on first startup
iDrive screen fails to boot or shows errors on startup
Multiple warning messages after jump-starting the 12V battery

citations.title: BMW i5 (2024) Owner's Manual - 12V vehicle battery, jump-starting, and emergency unlocking information

communityRecommendations.text: If you park the i5 in a garage, keep it plugged in even at 100% — it maintains the 12V battery. A dead 12V on a BMW EV is a flatbed tow to the dealer.

records.title: Acoustic Pedestrian Warning Sound Generator Fault (AVAS)
records.description: Under NHTSA recall 23V885000, certain 2024 i5 eDrive40 and i5 M60 vehicles have an external artificial sound generator (AVAS) control unit that can experience a fault at startup and fail to produce the legally required external pedestrian warning sound. Because EVs are nearly silent at low speed, a missing AVAS sound means pedestrians, cyclists, and the visually impaired may not hear the car approaching, increasing injury risk. This requirement is mandated in both the U.S. (FMVSS 141) and the EU (AVAS regulation), so it is directly relevant to EU-spec cars.
records.solution: Safety recall: the dealer (or OTA) updates the external artificial sound generator software at no charge. Owner notification letters were mailed February 16, 2024. Verify recall status by VIN.
symptoms: No external warning sound at low speed
AVAS / acoustic pedestrian protection warning message
Car is silent when creeping or reversing

records.title: Adaptive Suspension Self-Leveling Calibration Errors
records.description: Some BMW i5 owners report the adaptive air suspension displaying fault warnings and defaulting to a fixed ride height. The system's height sensors can lose calibration after software updates or battery disconnection, triggering a chassis malfunction warning.
records.solution: Perform a suspension calibration reset using BMW ISTA diagnostic software. If the issue persists, inspect the ride height sensors at each corner for damage or loose connectors. A dealer software update may also resolve the issue.
symptoms: Car lower than normal on one corner

records.title: A/C Wiring Harness Damaged During Cabin Filter Service (Short-Circuit/Fire Risk)
records.description: NHTSA recall 26V096000 (about 58,700 U.S. 2024-2026 i5 and 5 Series, ~337,000 worldwide) addresses the air-conditioning electrical wiring harness, which was routed too close to a housing-cover screw for the cabin air filter. During a routine cabin-filter replacement, the screw can pinch or damage the harness; a damaged harness can short-circuit and cause a thermal event (smoke or fire) even when the vehicle is parked and off. BMW opened the engineering investigation in March 2025 after several thermal events were reported. This is especially relevant to owners or independent shops doing DIY cabin-filter changes.
records.solution: Safety recall: the dealer inspects the harness, replaces it if damaged, and installs a protective retaining bracket to keep the screw away from the wiring, free of charge. Owner notification letters were expected April 13, 2026. Until repaired, avoid DIY cabin-filter replacement on affected VINs.
symptoms: Burning smell or smoke from dashboard area
A/C electrical fault after cabin filter change

records.title: DC Fast-Charge Throttling and Loud Cooling Fans on Repeated Sessions
records.description: Owners report that after several consecutive DC fast-charging sessions the i5 noticeably reduces its DC charging power as a battery-protection measure, with the reduction resetting after the pack cools (a few hours, longer with repeated fast charging). German motor-talk.de threads discuss reduced charging speed and BMW charging-curve product measures (Produktmaßnahme) for the xDrive40. Owners also report very loud cooling fans during and after DC charging plus charging amps randomly dropping and scheduled-charging sessions being skipped. While some thermal throttling is normal EV behavior, the abruptness and the loud thermal-management noise are common complaints, and BMW has shipped charging software updates to improve the curve.
records.solution: Keep the i5 on the latest software, since BMW has released charging-curve/charging-management updates via OTA and dealer flashes. Precondition the battery before fast charging to reduce throttling, avoid back-to-back DC sessions when possible, and report persistent amp drops or skipped scheduled charges to the dealer (some cases were traced to software faults). Loud thermal-management fan noise is generally normal during/after DC charging.
symptoms: Reduced DC charging power after multiple sessions
Scheduled charging skipped / sleeps through charge window
Very loud cooling fans during/after DC fast charging

records.title: Electric Drive Motor Software False Isolation Fault Causing Drive Power Loss
records.description: NHTSA recall 25V395000 (about 70,852 BMW EVs including the 2024 i5) addresses electric drive motor software that may incorrectly detect a double-isolation (HV insulation) fault. When triggered, the vehicle enters a fail-safe mode that shuts down the high-voltage system for roughly 15-20 seconds. Braking and steering remain available, but the car loses propulsion, which raises crash risk. This matches owner forum reports of 2024 i5s (notably M60) going inoperable after a drivetrain/software event, sometimes requiring a tow.
records.solution: Safety recall remedy is an electric drive motor software update, delivered over-the-air (OTA) or at the dealer, free of charge. Owner notification letters were scheduled for August 5, 2025. Keep the car on current software and verify recall completion by VIN.
symptoms: Sudden loss of drive power / propulsion
Drivetrain or hybrid system warning message
Vehicle becomes undriveable / requires tow in some cases

records.title: Heat-Pump Drip-Tube Thunking/Clunking Noise (Battery Pack Drop to Repair)
records.description: i5 owners widely report an intermittent low-level thunking, clacking, or banging noise coming from under the car, often while parked or after climate/charging activity. BMW traced it to the heat-pump A/C condensate drip tube: water collecting from the heat pump drips into the tube, and the length of the tube amplifies the drip into a knock that resonates through the body. Owners reported cars spending weeks at dealers before the cause was identified. BMW issued a service bulletin, but the repair is invasive because accessing the part requires dropping the high-voltage battery pack from the vehicle.
records.solution: Have the dealer perform the heat-pump drip-tube fix per the BMW service bulletin (a TSB exists). Note the repair typically requires lowering the HV battery pack to reach the component, so it is labor-intensive; it should be covered under the new-vehicle warranty. Reference the i5 forum thread and the bulletin when scheduling so the dealer does not misdiagnose.
symptoms: Low-level thunking / clacking / banging noise from underneath
Noise after running climate control or charging
Sporadic knock not tied to driving

records.title: High-Voltage Battery Module Insufficient Weld Seams (Overheat/Fire Risk)
records.description: NHTSA recall 24V135000 covers early-production 2024 i5 eDrive40 (alongside i4) vehicles whose high-voltage traction battery modules may contain insufficient weld seams. Specifically, the laser-welding process connecting the cell-contacting system to a cell terminal may not have been performed correctly, which can cause the battery module to overheat and increases the risk of fire. The U.S. campaign scope was very small (4 units, of which only one was in customer hands), but it is a genuine, NHTSA-documented HV battery manufacturing defect for the earliest cars.
records.solution: Safety recall: the dealer replaces the affected high-voltage battery module free of charge. Owners of very early 2024 i5 eDrive40 builds should verify recall status by VIN with BMW (1-800-525-7417) or at nhtsa.gov.

records.title: Integrated Brake System (IB) Servomotor Weld Failure
records.description: BMW recalled the i5 across multiple campaigns (NHTSA 24V104000, 24V697000, and 24V739000) for the electromechanical Integrated Brake (IB) system. In the servomotor weld campaign (24V697000), the welds joining the servomotor's hollow shaft inside the integrated brake control module may break. This can cause a loss of power brake (boost) assist and a loss of rear-axle braking, and the Antilock Brake System (ABS) and Dynamic Stability Control (DSC) may stop functioning. The defect was discovered during end-of-line testing in July 2024 and traced to improper welding of the servomotor shaft. The earlier 24V104000 and later 24V739000 campaigns address related IB module malfunctions producing the same brake-assist/ABS/DSC loss.
records.solution: This is a safety recall. The dealer replaces the complete Integrated Brake (IB) system / control module free of charge under the recall. Owners should verify their VIN against open recalls at nhtsa.gov or with BMW (1-800-525-7417); parts were reported available by i5 owners in late 2024.

records.title: Regenerative Braking Inconsistency in Cold Weather
records.description: The i5 exhibits noticeably reduced or inconsistent regenerative braking in cold weather (below 40°F / 4°C). When the battery is cold, the battery management system limits regen to protect the cells, which causes the car to coast much further than expected when lifting off the accelerator. The transition between reduced regen and full regen can be abrupt once the battery warms up, creating an inconsistent driving experience. One-pedal driving becomes unreliable in winter conditions.
records.solution: Use the BMW departure timer to precondition the battery before driving — this warms the battery and restores full regen capability from the start. Set the regen level to "Adaptive" instead of "High" in winter, which provides smoother transitions. BMW software updates have improved regen ramping behavior. Rely more on friction brakes during the first 10-15 minutes of cold-weather driving until the battery warms.
symptoms: Car coasts much further than expected when lifting off accelerator in cold weather
Regen braking strength changes abruptly during a drive
Range display showing higher consumption in cold weather
Regen indicator on dash showing reduced regeneration level

records.title: Steering Spindle Double Universal Joint Fracture
records.description: Under NHTSA recall 24V714000, certain i5 sedans were built with a steering-linkage spindle whose specifications 'may not have been appropriate for the application.' The swivel socket of the spindle's double universal joint can break, producing a sudden, unexpected increase in steering effort. Drivers may first notice noise from the steering column and changes in steering feel/behavior before failure. The U.S. campaign was small (about 202 i5 sedans) but the failure mode is serious because greater steering effort is required to control the car.
records.solution: Safety recall: the dealer replaces the steering spindle's double universal joint at no charge. Owner notification letters were mailed November 22, 2024. Owners noticing column noise or heavier steering should stop driving and contact BMW (1-800-525-7417) and verify recall status by VIN.
symptoms: Change in steering behavior or feel
